CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Mayor  www.SanMarinoCA.gov
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Steve Talt, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2024 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
300-0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00
  p.m. the day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will
  be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00

   p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council
  at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us
  teleconference module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted
  after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Talt, Vice Mayor Shepherd
Romey, and Mayor Huang

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.
PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.
CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

  PRESENTATION

 1.  RECEIVE AND FILE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT
  (ANNUAL AUDIT) FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that this annual financial statement be received
  and filed. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the audited financial statements for the fiscal year ended
  June 30, 2024.”

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 2 of 10
   PUBLIC HEARINGS

 2.  PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O-
  24-1416 AMENDING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS 23.01.01 AND
  23.02.25 TO IMPLEMENT STATE LAW REGARDING ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council conduct a public hearing and
  introduce for first reading Ordinance No. O-24-1416. If the City Council agrees, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to waive full reading and introduce by title only Ordinance No. O-24-1416,
  an Ordinance of the San Marino City Council amending Municipal Code Sections
  23.01.01 and 23.02.25 to implement State law regarding accessory dwelling units.”

 3.  PUBLIC HEARING IN CONSIDERATION OF:
  ADOPT AN ADDENDUM TO A NEGATIVE DECLARATION (SCH
  2022010208) AND ADOPT THE 2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT
  UPDATE (6TH CYCLE – AS AMENDED) OF THE SAN MARINO GENERAL
  PLAN AND UPDATE THE CITY’S OFFICIAL GENERAL LAND USE MAP;
  AND
  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. O-24-1415
  AMENDING THE CITY’S OFFICIAL ZONING MAP AND CODE SECTIONS
  23.01.01 (DEFINITIONS), 23.01.05 (ZONES AND AREA DISTRICTS
  ESTABLISHED, DELINEATION OF ZONES AND DISTRICTS ON ZONE
  MAP), 23.01.10 (REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION), 23.02.01 (USES
  PERMITTED), 23.03.01 (USES), 23.03.10 (STANDARDS FOR MULTI-
  FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT), 23.05.01 (USES PERMITTED
  AND CONDITIONALLY PERMITTED), 23.05.03 (STANDARDS FOR
  MULTI-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT), 23.06.04 (YARDS
  GENERALLY IN THE R-1 ZONE), 23.06.05 (GARAGES AND OTHER
  ACCESSORY BUILDINGS IN THE R-1 ZONE), 23.10.03 (NUMBER OF
  PARKING SPACES REQUIRED IN THE C-1 ZONE), 23.10.04 (PARKING
  REQUIREMENTS FOR USES NOT SPECIFIED IN THE C-1 ZONE),
  23.10.06 (REQUIRED IMPROVEMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF
  PARKING AREA IN THE C-1 ZONE), 23.15.04 (MATTERS SUBJECT TO
  DESIGN REVIEW), AND 23.15.16 (STANDARD OF REVIEW FOR
  APPLICATIONS NOT SUBJECT TO DESIGN REVIEW), AND CREATING
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS 23.05.04 (APPLICATION APPROVAL AND
  SUBMITTAL  REQUIREMENTS),  AND  23.05.05  (BY-RIGHT
  REQUIREMENTS), AMENDING ARTICLE 20 OF CHAPTER 23 (MULTI-
  FAMILY DWELLING ZONES), AND ADDING THE FOLLOWING ARTICLE
  TO CHAPTER 23: 1) ARTICLE 21 (MIXED-USE ZONES); 2) ARTICLE 22
  (DENSITY BONUS LAW); AND, 3) ARTICLE 23 (BY-RIGHT APPROVAL)
  TO BE CONSISTENT WITH THE GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 3 of 10
   AND RELATED UPDATES AND FINDING THAT ORDINANCE NO. O-24-
  1415 IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA PURSUANT TO CEQA GUIDELINES
  SECTION 15061(B)(3)

  Recommendation: In the case that the City Council considers approval of Resolution
  No. PR 24-29, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve Resolution No. PR 24-29, a resolution of the San Marino City
  Council adopting: 1) an Addendum to an adopted Initial Study/Negative Declaration;
  2) adoption of the City’s 6th Cycle Housing Element update consistent with the
  statutory requirements of the California Housing Element Law; 3) update to the
  General Plan Land Use map; and

  I move to waive full reading and introduce by title only Ordinance No. O-24-1415
  updating the City’s official zoning map and amending San Marino Municipal Code
  Article 20 of Chapter 23 and Sections 23.01.01, 23.01.05, 23.01.10, 23.03.01,
  23.03.10, 23.05.01, 23.05.03, 23.06.04, 23.06.05, 23.10.03, 23.10.04, 23.10.06,
  23.15.04, and 23.15.16, adding Municipal Code Section 23.05.04, and 23.05.05, and
  adding Articles 21, 22, and 23 to Chapter 23 of the Municipal Code; and finding that
  Ordinance No. O-24-1415 is exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section
  15061(b)(3).”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

 4.  INTRODUCTION FOR FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. O-24-1417
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN MARINO
  AMENDING SAN MARINO MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 2.06.03
  PERTAINING TO THE CITY MANAGER’S AUTHORITY TO PAY CLAIMS
  AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-24-36 DELEGATING CLAIMS
  SETTLEMENT AUTHORITY TO THE CITY MANAGER

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council introduce for first reading
  Ordinance No. O-24-1417 amending San Marino Municipal Code section 2.06.03 and
  approve Resolution No. R-24-36, delegating $30,000 in settlement/claims payment
  authority to the City Manager for non-CJPIA covered claims. If the City Council
  agrees, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to introduce Ordinance No. O-24-1417, an Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of San Marino Amending San Marino Municipal Code Section 2.06.03
  Pertaining to the City Manager’s Authority to Pay Claims for first reading by title only
  and waive further reading; and approve Resolution No. R-24-36.”

 5.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-24-37, A REVIEW OF THE SAN
  MARINO POLICE DEPARTMENT MILITARY EQUIPMENT ANNUAL
  REPORT AND RENEWAL OF SAN MARINO CITY ORDINANCE NO. O-22-
  1390

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 4 of 10
   Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution R-24-37 renewing
  San Marino City Ordinance O-22-1390 and finding that the annual Military Equipment
  Report 2024 complies with the standards of approval set forth in Government §§
  7070, 7071 and 7072. If Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution R-24-37 renewing San Marino City Ordinance O-22-1390
  and finding that the annual Military Equipment Report 2024 complies with the
  standards of approval set forth in Government §§ 7070, 7071 and 7072.”

 6.  APPROVAL  OF  AMENDED  AND  RESTATED  CITY  MANAGER
  EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT, CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-
  24-31 AMENDING JOB CLASSIFICATIONS AND APPROVING THE JOB
  CLASSIFICATION FOR THE POSITION OF PART-TIME BUILDING
  ATTENDANT, CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-24-30
  APPROVING THE UPDATED SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FY 2024-2025,
  AND CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-24-34 AMENDING THE
  UNREPRESENTED EMPLOYEES SALARY AND BENEFITS SCHEDULE FOR
  THE PERIOD COVERING JULY 1, 2024, THROUGH JUNE 30, 2027, TO
  INCLUDE THE POSITION OF PART-TIME BUILDING ATTENDANT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve an amended and
  restated City Manager Employment Agreement with Philippe Eskandar, approve
  necessary budget amendments, adopt Resolution No. R-24-31 amending job
  classifications and approving the classification for the position of part-time Building
  Attendant, adopt Resolution No. R-24-30 approving the updated Salary Schedule for
  FY 2024-2025, adopt Resolution No. R-24-34 amending the Unrepresented
  Employees Salary and Benefits Schedule for the period covering July 1, 2024,
  through June 30, 2027, to include the position of part-time Building Attendant. If the
  City Council agrees, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the amended and restated City Manager Employment Agreement
  with Philippe Eskandar, approve necessary budget amendments, adopt Resolution
  No. R-24-31 amending job classifications and approving the classification for the
  position of part-time Building Attendant, adopt Resolution No. R-24-30 approving the
  updated Salary Schedule for FY 2024-2025, and adopt Resolution No. R-24-34
  amending the Unrepresented Employees Salary and Benefits Schedule for the period
  covering July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2027, to include the position of part-time
  Building Attendant.”

 7.  AWARD OF 3-YEAR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENTS TO JOHN
  L HUNTER AND ASSOCIATES, AND DUDEK IN A TOTAL AMOUNT NOT
  TO  EXCEED  $150,000  EACH  FOR  ON-CALL  STORMWATER
  ENGINEERING SERVICES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2027

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council award professional services
  agreements for on-call stormwater engineering services to John L Hunter and
  Associates and Dudek. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 5 of 10
   “I move to award a three-year professional services agreement for on-call
  stormwater engineering services to John L Hunter and Associates and Dudek through
  June 30, 2027, with total contract values not to exceed $150,000 each.”

 8.  APPROVAL  OF  AMENDMENTS  TO  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES
  AGREEMENTS WITH TRANSTECH ENGINEERS AND HARTZOG &
  CRABILL IN TOTAL AMOUNTS OF $50,000 AND $100,000 FOR ON-
  CALL TRAFFIC ENGINEERING SERVICES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2026.

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendments No. 1 to
  both Professional Services Agreements with Transtech and HCI, increasing the total
  compensation amounts by $50,000 and $100,000, respectively, for the duration of
  the agreements. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve Amendments No. 1 to the Professional Services Agreements with
  Transtech Engineers and Hartzog & Crabill increasing the total compensation
  amounts by $50,000 and $100,000, respectively, for the duration of the
  agreements.”

 9.  AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH RAFTELIS
  TO CONDUCT A SEWER RATE STUDY IN THE AMOUNT OF $52,949 &
  AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT TO REVENUE &
  COST SPECIALISTS (RCS) TO CONDUCT THE COST ALLOCATION PLAN
  & CITYWIDE FEE STUDY IN THE AMOUNT OF $29,750

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council award a Professional Services
  Agreement with Raftelis to conduct a Sewer Rate Study in an amount not to exceed
  $52,949. and approve a budget amendment of $52,949 in the General Fund to cover
  the cost of the study. If Council agrees with Staff’s recommendation a motion would
  be:

  “I move to authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with Raftelis to conduct
  a Sewer Rate Study, in the amount not to exceed $52,949 and approve the FY 24/25
  budget amendment to appropriate $52,949 in the General Fund.”

  Staff also recommends the Council award a Professional Services Agreement with
  Revenue & Cost Specialists (RCS)to conduct a Cost Allocation Plan and City-wide Fee
  Study in an amount not to exceed $29,750. If Council agrees with Staff’s
  recommendation a motion would be:

  “I move to authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with Revenue & Cost
  Specialists (RCS) to conduct a Cost Allocation Plan and City-wide Fee Study in an
  amount not to exceed $29,750.”

 10. AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT TO NICHOLS

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 6 of 10
   CONSULTING ENGINEERS FOR THE PREPARATION OF PLANS,
  SPECIFICATIONS AND COST ESTIMATES FOR THE DESIGN OF
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDED FY 2024-
  25 ADA SIDEWALK CURB RAMP PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $47,195

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council award a Professional
  Services Agreement to NCE in the amount of $47,195 to prepare plans,
  specifications, and cost estimates for the Community Development Block Grant
  funded FY 2024-25 ADA Sidewalk Curb Ramp Project. Staff also recommends the
  budget appropriations to account for the additional CDBG funding expected in FY
  2024-25 for this project. The budget appropriations necessary are an increase to
  revenue account #204-00-3201-0650 in the amount of $133,406 and an increase to
  expenditure account #204-48-4600-9272 in the amount of $133,406. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to award a Professional Services Agreement to NCE in the amount of
  $47,195 to prepare plans, specifications, and cost estimates for the Community
  Development Block Grant funded FY 2024-25 ADA Sidewalk Curb Ramp Project,
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on behalf of the City, and
  approve budget appropriations necessary.”

 11. APPROVAL OF PURCHASE OF ELECTRIC RIDING MOWER FOR THE
  PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $35,062.99 AND APPROPRIATION OF $4,622.97 FOR THE PURCHASE

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the purchase of one
  electric riding mower from La Verne Power Equipment, Inc., in the amount of
  $35,062.99, and authorize the budget appropriations necessary for the purchase as
  listed below:
  • A transfer out from the General Fund 101 of $4,622.97 to the Capital
  Equipment Fund 591
  • Also needed is an increase of $4,622.97 into Fund 591
  Account # 591-50-4613-0000

  If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion
  would be:
  “I move to approve the purchase of one electric riding mower from La Verne Power
  Equipment, Inc., in the amount of $35,062.99, and authorize the necessary budget
  appropriations for the purchase.”

 12. APPOINTMENT OF ADVISORY BODY MEMBERS TO THE RECREATION
  COMMISSION AND LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES

  Recommendation: The Council Liaisons for the Recreation Commission recommend
  the Council appointment of three (3) regular members to serve three-year terms
  each commencing on November 13, 2024.

  The Council Liaisons for the Library Board of Trustees recommend the Council
  appointment of one (1) alternate member to serve a partial term commencing on
  November 13, 2024.

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 7 of 10
   If Council concurs, the appropriate motions would be:

  “I move to appoint Victor Chang, David Raichlen, and Tammie Ton as regular
  members of the Recreation Commission to serve terms ending May 31, 2028.”

  “I move to appoint Marilyn Peck as an alternate member of the Library Board of
  Trustees to serve a partial term to end on May 31, 2026.”

 13. APPROVAL OF 2025 LACY PARK MAJOR SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT
  DATES AND CO-SPONSORSHIP REQUESTS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the 2025 Lacy Park
  Special Event Permit Dates and Fee Requests. It the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation an appropriate motion would be:

  "I move to approve the 2025 Lacy Park Special Event Permit Dates and Co-
  Sponsorship Requests.”

 14. APPROVAL OF FY 2024-2025 CAPITAL EQUIPMENT RE-BUDGET AND
  BUDGET AMENDMENT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that Council approve the increase in
  expenditures of $109,938 in account #591-34-4613-9300 and the increase in
  revenues of $50,000 in account #591-00-3702-0000 for the expected FY 2024-2025
  reimbursement. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the requested updates to the FY 2024-2025 budget.”

 15. FALL 2024 PUBLIC TREE REMOVAL LIST

  Recommendation: This is an informational item. Therefore, no action is required by
  City Council.

 16. APPROVAL OF CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY CLOSURE CALENDAR FOR
  2025

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approval of the Crowell Public
  Library closure calendar for 2025. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Crowell Public Library closure calendar for 2025.”

 17. RATIFICATION OF THE FY 2023-24 CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY
  REPORT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council ratify the FY 2023-24 California

AGENDA – NOVEMBER 13, 2024  PAGE 8 of 10
   State Library Report. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to ratify the FY 2023-24 California State Library Report.”

 18. APPROVAL OF FRANCHISE TAX BOARD DATA SHARING AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the FTB Data Sharing
  Agreement and direct the City Manager to execute the agreement and future
  extensions as needed. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Franchise Tax Board Data Sharing Agreement and direct the
  City Manager to execute the agreement and future extensions as needed.”

 19. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF SEPTEMBER
  2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of
  September 2024.”

 20. RECEIVE AND  FILE  MONTHLY  DISBURSEMENTS  REPORT  FOR
  OCTOBER 2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of October 2024. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of
  October 2024.”

 21. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the October 2024
  minutes. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of October 9, 2024, the
  regular meeting of October 9, 2024, and the adjourned regular meeting of October
  25, 2024.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
